thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PAGER fired for AUTH-TOKEN-VERIFY (sev2). Trigger: token-verify-high-error-rate. Links: https://pd.example/PN12345
alex: acked. I'm on it, grabbing logs.
maria: seeing a spike in token verification errors from api-gateway-us-east-1. 500s on /v1/auth/verify. Rate ~1200/min.
josh: any customer reports? sara (support): getting a DM from AcmeCorp saying 'authentication failing for many users'—they're seeing 401s in their app.
alex: adding context: alerts show a surge of kid-not-found errors in auth-service logs. Sample log:
```
ERROR auth.verifier: kid not found in JWKS: kid=3fb9c2
request_id=abc123
```
maria: confirmed. JWKS fetch from our keys cache returns older payload without the new key that signing-service pushed 5m ago.
incident-bot: NOTE: automatic fallback attempted: local cached key set used. Fallback success rate 0% (no match) :warning:
josh: seems like key rotation propagation flapping. Could be caching TTL or CDN in front of JWKS endpoint.
sara (support): customer impact - multiple tenants reporting login failures; estimated affected sessions: ~25% of active tokens past 24h.
alex: I'm spinning up a hotfix: force-refresh JWKS on all verifier pods and disable caching for 2m. Doing canary to 3 pods now.
maria: rolling command:
```
kubectl exec -n auth $(kubectl get pod -l app=auth-verifier -o name | head -n3) -- /bin/sh -c "curl -sSf https://keys.internal/jwks || true; pkill -HUP verifier"
```
josh: +1. Also patching our JWKS caching library to accept overlapping keys during rotation (tolerate unknown kid for 30s by trying last-known keys).
pagerduty-bot: Reminder: if incident exceeds 30m escalate to oncall-rotation-2. Current elapsed 8m.
alex: rolling to 12 pods now. Logs after refresh show decrease in kid-not-found errors on those pods.
maria: traffic split shows those pods drop error rate to ~1%. Cluster-wide still 18%.
josh: can we roll a config that temporarily allows verifying tokens by trying both current & previous key sets? that requires a signing key id mapping update.
alex: yes, deploying verifier change that loads 2 JWKS versions: current + previous. Pushing container build now.
sara (support): letting AcmeCorp know we're working on key propagation and temporary workaround. Sending interim status: 'engineers investigating; mitigation in progress'.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: ack by alex. Next reminder in 10m if unacknowledged.
alex: build passed. Deploying to prod with gradual rollout (5 -> 25 -> 100%).
maria: during rollout, observed a weird 502 spike from edge when pods restarted; throttling rollout to 10% and increasing probes.
josh: getting a few reports of tokens signed with new kid failing because older key wasn't present in signing-service's published JWKS—possible race where signing-service rotated before publishing.
alex: reached out to signing-service owner in #eng-runtime: @rachel can you confirm JWKS publishing happened atomically with rotation?
alex: rachel? ping.
rachel: saw rotation job run and publish event failed due to flaky s3 write; it's currently retrying. Pushing immediate republish attempt.
maria: republish successful at ts=2505009910.
incident-bot: JWKS cache invalidation triggered across regions.
alex: errors across cluster dropped to <0.5% after republish and verifier patch. Rolling to 100%.
sara (support): update sent to AcmeCorp: 'Issue mitigated; tokens should authenticate normally now. Please re-open if you see further 401s.'
josh: root cause: signing-service rotation with failed publish + tight JWKS cache TTL causing transient islanded verifiers. Follow-ups: 1) improve signing-service publish retry logic 2) add gradual key rollout (publish prev+new before switch) 3) extend JWKS cache TTL + allow graceful fallback to previous key set 4) add synthetic check after rotation to validate fetch success.
alex: creating follow-up ticket and linking to this thread.
incident-bot: Incident declared resolved by alex. Total duration ~14m. Severity lowered to sev3 for follow-ups.
alex: handoff to oncall team for postmortem: @oncall-next please pick this up for RCA.
oncall-next: acknowledged. I'll draft postmortem and coordinate with rachel and runtime.
sara (support): closing customer loop with ACME; requesting email confirmation when they see normal behavior.
alex: thanks everyone. adding notes to incident board and scheduling blameless postmortem.
